{{Short description|Inequality relating to the Laplace operator}}

In [[functional analysis]], a subfield of mathematics, '''Kato's inequality''' is a [[Distribution (mathematics)|distributional]] inequality for the [[Laplace operator]] or certain [[elliptic operator]]s. It was proven in 1972 by the Japanese mathematician [[Tosio Kato]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=Tosio| last=Kato |title=Schrödinger operators with singular potentials |journal=  [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]|volume=13 |date=1972 | issue=1–2 |pages=135–148 |doi=10.1007/BF02760233| s2cid=115546931 }}</ref>

The original inequality is for some degenerate elliptic operators.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Allen |last=Devinatz |title=On an Inequality of Tosio Kato for Degenerate-Elliptic Operators |journal=Journal of Functional Analysis |volume=32 |number=3 |date=1979 |pages=312–335 |doi=10.1016/0022-1236(79)90043-0|doi-access=free }}</ref> This article treats the special (but important) case for the Laplace operator.<ref name="BrezisPonce">{{cite journal |first1=Haı̈m |last1=Brezis |first2=Augusto |last2=Ponce |title= Kato's inequality when Δu is a measure|journal= Comptes Rendus Mathematique|volume=338 |date=2004 |issue=8 |pages=599–604 |doi=10.1016/j.crma.2003.12.032|url=http://www.numdam.org/articles/10.1016/j.crma.2003.12.032/ |hdl=2078.1/70476 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Inequality for the Laplace operator ==
Let <math>\Omega\subset \R^d</math> be a bounded and [[open set]], and <math>f\in L^1_{\operatorname{loc}}(\Omega)</math> such that <math>\Delta f\in L^1_{\operatorname{loc}}(\Omega)</math>. Then the following holds<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |first1=Wolfgang |last1=Arendt |first2=Antonious F.M. |last2=ter Elst |publisher=Springer |title=Kato's Inequality |encyclopedia=Analysis and Operator Theory. Springer Optimization and Its Applications |series=Springer Optimization and Its Applications |volume =146 |place=Cham |date=2019 |pages=47–60 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-12661-2_3|isbn=978-3-030-12660-5 |s2cid=191796248 }}</ref><ref name="BrezisPonce" />
:<math>\Delta |f| \geq \operatorname{Re}\left((\operatorname{sgn}\overline f) \Delta f\right)\quad</math> in <math>\;\mathcal{D}'(\Omega)</math>,

where
:<math>\operatorname{sgn}\overline f=\begin{cases}\frac{\overline{f(x)}}{|f(x)|} & \text{if }f\neq 0\\
0 & \text{if }f=0.
\end{cases}</math><ref>{{cite journal |first=Toshio |last=Horiuchi |title=Some remarks on Kato's inequality |journal=Journal of Inequalities and Applications |date=2001 |volume=2001 |page=615789 |doi=10.1155/S1025583401000030 |doi-access= free}}</ref>
<math>L^1_{\operatorname{loc}}</math> is the space of [[locally integrable function]]s – i.e., functions that are [[Integrable function|integrable]] on every [[Compact subset|''compact'' subset]] of their [[Domain of definition|domains of definition]].

=== Remarks ===
* Sometimes the inequality is stated in the form
::<math>\Delta f^+ \geq \operatorname{Re}\left(1_{[f\geq 0]} \Delta f\right)\quad</math> in <math>\;\mathcal{D}'(\Omega)</math>
: where <math>f^+=\operatorname{max}(f,0)</math> and <math>1_{[f\geq 0]}</math> is the [[indicator function]].
* If <math>f</math> is continuous in <math>\Omega</math> then
::<math>\Delta |f| \geq \operatorname{Re}\left((\operatorname{sgn}\overline f) \Delta f\right)\quad</math> in <math>\;\mathcal{D}'(\{f\neq 0\})</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Juan|last1=Dávila |first2=Augusto |last2=Ponce |date=2003|title=Variants of Kato's inequality and removable singularities|journal=[[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]] |volume=91 |pages=143–178|doi=10.1007/BF02788785|s2cid=55929478 |hdl=2078.1/70502 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
